canonical_topic: Weak correlation between coal and electricity prices
definition: Even though coal's primary use is electricity generation, coal and power prices are generally not correlated because power prices are set by the marginal (most expensive) fuel in a region, not the cheapest.
core_idea: Electricity prices are typically driven by the most expensive fuel used in a region rather than by coal, so the coal-power price relationship is weak except in limited cases.
key_points: Coal is primarily used for electrical generation, but coal and electricity prices are usually not correlated except in limited cases
Electricity prices are generally set by the most expensive fuel in a region, not the cheapest fuel (which is often coal)
Only investors who own coal-fired power plants can actually capture value from the coal-to-electricity price spread
relationships: Relates to merit-order/marginal-fuel price setting in power markets
trading_implications: The coal-electricity spread is effectively only monetizable by owners of coal-fired generation assets, not general market participants
caveats: Assuming coal prices and electricity prices move together because coal is a major generation fuel
